newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-Taiwan GDRs rebound, lifted by locals.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-Taiwan GDRs rebound, lifted by locals.

text.p: Taiwanese global depository receipts surged on Friday, more than regaining heavy losses endured on Thursday, as local liquidity buoyed shares, traders said.
They said that an extremely strong local market was carrying GDRs along in its wake, despite concerns by foreign investors about heady valuations.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index shot 3.60 points higher to 140.73, representing a discount to the local market of 2.69 percent.
Taiwan's share index set a seven-year high at the close, gaining 105.6 points, or 1.1 percent, to end at 9,677.4.
"Electronic sharers were quite strong, but I'm really not sure clients are convinced," a trader said.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index closed 0.56 points lower at 84.31, a 0.66 percent rise, with the premium over the local market at 20.54 percent from 19.90 percent.
Reliance gained six cents to $21.25/$22.25 and Hindalco fell 12 cents to $31.87/$32.87.
Bombay's benchmark index fell 68.80 points to 4,124.81.
The HSBC James Capel Korea GDR Index gained 0.65 points firmer, rising to 75.81 points, a premium of 43.17 percent over the local market.
